turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Rohan, come inside. Your pressure is one twenty eight over seventy eight and the pulse is seventy four, I have put it on the slip.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sit. What is it today?

[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Doctor, I came to ask whether I can start driving again. I am having epilepsy since six years, the fits, and I am on levipil, they told me not to drive, but it has been quiet since two years so I wanted to check properly before I touch the car.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Last convulsion?

[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): The last proper fit was around two years back, March or April I think, umm, I cannot pin the date. Since that day there has been no jerking and no tongue bite, nothing of that sort.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Levipil dose?

[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): It is levetiracitam, five hundred mg, morning and night, always after food, because empty stomach used to make me feel heavy. The neurologist started it six years back and the dose itself was never changed.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any reaction to a medicine? Rash, swelling?
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): No, never, I have taken penicillin and everything, no problem at all. Even the pain tablets after my tooth was pulled, I was completely fine.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. Two years clear, no blood test. You can drive. Come back in one year.

[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): Umm, before you close it, my sister saw a blank spell last month. We were talking after dinner and she said I stopped mid sentence and just stared, only for a few seconds. I myself have no memory of it, and which date exactly I cannot say.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fall? Any jerking?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): No fall, no jerking, she said I just went blank and then carried on as if nothing happened. I felt a bit odd afterwards, but I put it down to tiredness from the journey.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Missed any tablets?

[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, when I went outstation to Pune for my cousin's wedding I missed the night dose, err, two or three times, because the bag was in the other room and I slept off. Normally I am very particular, morning and night, but those days I slipped.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Then no. Hold the driving. I will arrange a blood test.
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): Oh. So the driving is stopped then, even though the big fits have stayed away since two years.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Family. Any fits, sugar, pressure?

[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): My father had diabetes in his fifties, on tablets for sugar till he passed. My mother did not, no sugar, she is quite well even now. Another sister, uh my younger sister, has pressure but no sugar, she takes a small tablet for BP. My brother and the cousins, no fits in them at all.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Job? Do you drink?

[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): I am an accounts officer in a private firm, and the hours are nine to six, though in audit it stretches till eight or even nine. Diet is mostly home food, rice and dal and sabzi, outside food maybe twice a week. I walk twenty minutes in the morning, no gym or anything. Alcohol I don't take regularly, only one peg at a wedding, not even every month.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any weakness? Walk to the door.
[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): No weakness at all, I walk every morning on the colony road, same as this.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Gait is normal. No limb weakness.
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): So was that blank thing a fit, doctor? I really did not feel one myself.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): It may have been a small seizure, with those missed doses. I cannot be sure.
[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): Then even the office run is off? It is only four kilometres.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): No driving till I see you again. Do not skip a single dose. Blood test this week, levetiracetam level.
[SEG0029] person_3 (PATIENT): I can go Saturday before office. Do I skip that morning tablet for the test?
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Take it as usual. Come back in two weeks with the report.
[SEG0031] person_1 (NURSE): I will book that blood test at the desk. Collect the slip on the way out.

spec.situation: Adult with epilepsy on levetiracetam, seizure-free for two years, asks about driving; missed doses when travelling; relative saw a 'blank spell' last month; doctor reviews and plans a blood test.

traps.happens: The doctor asks about drug reactions. Variants (use ONE per encounter): (a) the patient says 'No, never, I have taken penicillin and everything' (no allergy); (b) the patient is unsure ('maybe the antibiotic or the painkiller, nobody told me which'); (c) a real allergy with the reaction described; (d) allergies are never asked.
traps.label_rule: (a) NO allergy entry: negative_findings 'Allergies' absent. (b) allergy with status uncertain, the substance as described, the reaction if said, plus an allergy_uncertain uncertainty. (c) allergy with the reaction. (d) nothing at all. NEVER list a medicine the patient has taken without a reaction as an allergy, and the plan must not prescribe a drug of a recorded allergy's family.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

features: doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

omissions.text: Patient reported no tongue bite with the last/proper fit and no tongue bite since then.
Levetiracetam is taken morning and night after food because taking it on an empty stomach made him feel heavy.
Levetiracetam dose has never been changed since it was started six years ago by a neurologist.
Allergy history was more specific: no reaction to medicines including no rash or swelling, and he has tolerated penicillin and pain tablets previously.
The witnessed blank spell occurred while talking after dinner; he stopped mid-sentence, stared for a few seconds, then carried on as if nothing had happened.
Patient denied memory of the blank spell himself.
After the blank spell he felt a bit odd afterwards, which he had attributed to tiredness from travel.

Patient admitted missing two or three night doses of levetiracetam while out of town in Pune for his cousin's wedding because the bag was in another room and he fell asleep; normally he is very particular with morning and night dosing.
Doctor initially said, before hearing about the blank spell, 'Two years clear, no blood test. You can drive. Come back in one year,' but then reversed this after the additional history.
Family history negatives/additional details: mother has no diabetes and is well; brother and cousins have no fits/epilepsy; sister has hypertension but no diabetes.
Patient denied weakness and doctor observed gait normal with no limb weakness after asking him to walk.
